text:
A: Hiya! Oh, you're the West Brom shirt. I clocked that in the photos, I was like, he looks like a laugh.
B: Ha, guilty, mate. Mark. Brierley Hill. And you're, er, Kerry, is it?
A: Kerry, yeah. Swindon. Don't say anything about the Magic Roundabout, everyone does.
B: I wasn't going to! I was, actually. Is it as bad as they say?
A: Honestly, it's fine once you know it. It's the A419 that's the nightmare. I'm on it every day for work and it's just, do you know what I mean, cones for the sake of cones.
B: Oh, don't. Round Merry Hill they've had the road up that long, I reckon the cones have got their own postcode. What is it you do, then?
A: Business development for a building and roofing supplier. So trade accounts, contractors, chasing new business across Wiltshire and Gloucestershire. Basically I'm the one who gets the big accounts in. It's a lot of phone, bit of site visits, showroom. I'm good at it, to be fair, I just think they don't pay what it's worth.
B: Nobody ever does, do they. Sounds like you can talk, anyway.
A: I can talk, yeah. Did a negotiation skills course last year and the bloke running it said I was a natural. So.
B: There you go then. I'd have been rubbish at that, I just chat. I was on a depot, picking and loading, but the back went, so I'm off now. Just had a lad on before you, Craig, same thing, back's gone. We was swapping notes like two old crocks.
A: Oh no. My back's not great either, to be honest, it's why I don't really do the gym. That's my excuse anyway.
B: That's a good excuse, I'd keep that one.
A: Ha! I've had three memberships. Dan, my husband, says I just pay them a direct debit to feel guilty.
B: Julie says the same about my darts. I'm on the team down the local, Thursdays. She says it's not a sport if you can do it with a pint in your hand.
A: She's not wrong though, is she?
B: She is not, no.
A: Have you been watching The Traitors? Everyone at work's obsessed.
B: Julie has it on. I sort of half watch it with my tea and then ask who's who and she gets the hump.
A: Oh, I'd get the hump. Last night was unreal. I'd be so good on that, I can read people, it's literally my job. I'd be a traitor, obviously.
B: Obviously! I'd be banished first week, me, I can't keep me face straight.
A: You've got an honest face, to be fair.
B: That's what the darts lads say before I take their money. Got any kids, Kerry?
A: Erm, no. No. We've got Biscuit, he's a cockapoo, he's basically the kid. He chewed my new trainers last week, sixty quid.
B: Oh, they do, don't they. My Roxy's too old to chew now, she just snores. I've got two grown up, and the grandkids. Off to Towyn with them next weekend in the caravan.
A: Aw, Towyn. I couldn't do a caravan, I'm more all-inclusive, Tenerife, Turkey. Went to Dubai a couple of years ago, that was something else.
B: Dubai, eh? Bit posh for me, mate. Give me a pint by a pool in Benidorm and I'm happy.
A: Nothing wrong with that. Bit of sun, cocktail, done.
B: Exactly, that's all you want, ain't it. Life's too short.
A: It is. That's what I keep telling Dan when he looks at the bank statements.
B: Ha! Julie does the statements in our house. I'm not allowed near.
A: Probably for the best, honestly.
